special_instructions.verbatim: (1) A/C configuration, in every sortie, is determined by the syllabus. SP always occupies the front seat, except for a ferry flight.
(2) All maneuvers that have not been practiced in the F/S will be demonstrated in the air at least once by IP, before SP is asked to execute them.

(3) SP will not fly SOLO if he/she has been graded with 59% or less in the previous flight, regardless of the Training Category. SP will continue his/her training on a Dual sortie in the Training Category in which he/she was graded “ALMOST GOOD” or “FAIL”. The SOLO will be flown in another flight of the same Training Section or in the following one, if applicable.

(4) SP will not fly SOLO, past four (4) calendar days since the last dual VFR flight that he/she flew from the front seat (the day he/her flew dual is not included) and provided that he/she has achieved at least MIF «2» in normal landing.
(5) In all missions, planning and execution will be made in such a way, so that the best A/C energy management is achieved.

(6) The following maneuvers ARE FORBIDDEN to be executed in SOLO flights: (a) All kind of STALLS. (b) SPINS (including Spin Prevention) (c) Unusual Attitudes. (d) ELP. (e) Straight in approach. (f) Slow Flight. (g) No Flap Overhead Patterns/ Landings (h) Simulated Lost Wingman Procedures.
(7) AGSM will be executed for warm-up and body preparation, in any flight that pre-planned maneuvering will load the A/C with more than 3 Gs.
(8) Special requirements will be separately annotated in the Grade-Sheet and the corresponding levels of performance will be given.

(9) In the program analysis of Training Units (“Analytical description of Section exercise”) and next to each maneuver, in parenthesis, the MINIMUM NUMBER of maneuvers that SP must practice until the end of a Training Section, appear. In case that the minimum number is not achieved SP will be granted an extra sortie or he/she will cover the required items in the next Section according to Squadron Commander’s judgment.

(10) Whenever there is no minimum number next to a maneuver in the Program Analysis, but the MIF for this maneuver is bigger in this Training Section than the previous one, then the maneuver should be practiced as much as required for the MIF to be achieved.

(11) In maneuvers where no grading is determined in the Training Section (i.e. Instrument approach in Contact), SP will be graded according to the criteria of the corresponding Training Section in which he/she currently flies, provided that the maneuver had been analyzed and briefed before flight. The maneuver will be annotated in the Grade Sheet along with the corresponding MIF. In any other case, SP will not be graded, but the maneuver will be annotated in the Grade Sheet as having been demonstrated by IP.

(1) Sortie C4101 will not be graded in the General performance (NG), except in case of an Air Sickness; in this case SP performance will be graded as “FAIR” (59%), will NOT fly an FCJ and continue at the next block.

(2) Up to “PRE-SOLO” phase, SP will be scheduled and fly maximum one (1) A/C and one (1) F/S sortie daily, apart from the instance of an aborting mission, after becoming airborne, due to adverse weather or A/C malfunction (MIC).

(3) In order to adequately monitor SPs progress in Contact Category, the listed below EVALUATIONS apply: C4590, C4790, C5090 and C5490 (FINAL CHECKRIDE). Evaluation Sorties will be executed from IP evaluators according to B.O. 3-1/ATC.
(4) Both C4790 and C4791 sorties will be flown the same day, with the same A/C.
(5) The evaluator of the C4790 will supervise and grade SP’s landing from the Contact Car.
(6) Nose -high unusual attitude recovery will initially be taught as pre-planned maneuver. After SP achieves MIF “1”, recoveries will be practiced from different attitudes without previous planning.
(7) In case that the MINIMUM NUMBER of maneuvers is not achieved at the end of the block, it must be annotated in the grade sheet and executed at the next block.
(8) ELPs will be performed daytime and under VMC conditions only.
a. SP will practice one landing with more than 750 Lbs. of fuel on board (SRC-6).
1. At the SOLO sortie, SP will perform one airport traffic pattern within the airport ATZ and one normal landing.
RESTRICTIONS: Minimum A/C fuel for the 1st SOLO is 550 lbs. (LAP 10-18 and 3-20).
SP will practice No Flaps overhead traffic pattern, as well as straight in and Landings with more than 750 LBS of fuel and. (SRC-6)

3. at the «SOLO» flight: a. SP will fly in a local area where he will practice the following, provided that he / she has achieved code MIF «2» in the previous dual contact sortie: (1) Aileron Roll. (2) Chandelle. (3) Lazy «8».
c. Any maneuver permitted for SOLO, in which he / she achieved MIF «2» at the previous dual contact sortie.
c. Any maneuver allowed for SOLO, in which he / she achieved MIF «2» at the previous dual contact sortie.

flags: PDF pages 174 (printed -166-) and 180 (printed -172-) are completely blank in the source PDF (no text, no images, no vector drawings) — verified with PyMuPDF; no Contact content is missing between C4601-02→C4790-91 and C4901-05→C5090.

Section keys follow the MIF unit labels of D:\FDMS\data\mif\t6a.json (tables contact_presolo_t6a / contact_t6a). The syllabus itself prints the generic forms C41ΧΧ, C42ΧΧ, C43ΧΧ, C44ΧΧ, C4590, C46XX, C4790–C4791, C48XX, C49XX, C5090, C51XX, C52XX, C53XX, C5490.

Combined printed lines of the form 'X - Y. (a) – (b)' (e.g. 'Chandelle - Lazy «8». (4) – (4)') were split into two maneuver entries sharing the identical verbatim string; the first number belongs to the first maneuver, the second to the second, exactly as printed.

'Power οn / ELP Stalls. (a) / (b)' split into 'Power on Stalls' (a) and 'ELP Stalls' (b); both map to the single MIF row sn 8 'Power ON / ELP Stalls'. The source prints a Greek omicron in 'οn' — preserved verbatim.

'Spin Prevention / Recovery. (a) / (b)' split into 'Spin Prevention' and 'Spin Recovery'; both map to the single MIF row sn 10 'Spin Prevention / Spin Recovery'. In C4301-03 only 'Spin Prevention. (3)' is printed (no recovery number).

Lines of the form 'X overhead traffic pattern and landing. (n)' carry ONE printed number covering both pattern and landing. Stored as a SINGLE entry whose min_number is mapped to the PATTERN MIF row (mif_sn 23 / 25 / 27 / 32); the corresponding LANDING row (24 / 26 / 28 / 33) is recorded in 'mif_sn_also' so the one printed number stays traceable from the landing row WITHOUT being counted twice. Exception: C4201-03 prints them separately ('Normal overhead traffic pattern. (12)' and 'Normal landing. (12)') — two independent entries, no mif_sn_also.
C4301-03: 'ELP and ELP landing (touch n’go). (2)' — one printed number covers two MIF rows; mapped to mif_sn 30 (ELP) with mif_sn_also [31] (ELP Landing).
C4101 (PDF 167), C4590 (PDF 172), C5090 (PDF 181) and C5490 (PDF 189) contain NO parenthetical minimum numbers — familiarization sortie and the three checkrides; maneuvers arrays intentionally empty.
C4401-03 prints 'Straight - in.' with NO number (unlike C4301-03 which prints '(1)') — not recorded, per rule 1. C4801-04 and C5101-02 print no Straight-in line at all.

'per' is 'section' for every Program Analysis number, per General Directive (9) (PDF 164): the number is the minimum SP must practice UNTIL THE END OF A TRAINING SECTION, not per sortie. No Contact line in the Program Analysis defines a per-sortie minimum.

special_instructions uses an extra scope value 'section' (with an added 'section' key) for per-section SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS / RESTRICTIONS / SOLO prerequisites (SRC-6 landing >750 lbs, 1st SOLO pattern+landing, 550 lbs fuel minimum, and the MIF «2» prerequisite for SOLO maneuvers in C4901-05 / C5201-04 / C5301-04). Consumers expecting only 'category'/'phase' can filter these out safely.

Header/table discrepancies in the source: C48XX header reads 'SORTIES/HOURS TOTAL: 4/4, 9' with 3 dual + 1 solo, C49XX header 'TOTAL: 5/6,2' with 4 dual + 1 solo, C52XX and C53XX headers 'TOTAL: 4 / 4.6' with 3 dual + 1 solo — consistent with the mission table on PDF 166. Not altered.

Typography preserved verbatim: 'Barel Roll' (sic; MIF row is 'Barrel Roll'), 'touch n’go', guillemets «8» / «S», en dash in 'Straight–in' (C4901-05) vs hyphen elsewhere, and missing final periods in 'TP Stalls (2)' (C4801-04), 'Flaps T/O overhead traffic pattern and landing (3)' (C4601-02) and '(1)' (C4790-91), 'Straight-In (1)' (C5201-04).
Section names as printed in the syllabus differ slightly from the MIF row names; mif_row values are the MIF table row names, name values are the syllabus wording.

special_instructions selection criterion: ALL of GENERAL DIRECTIVES (1)-(11) (PDF 163-164) and ALL of CONTACT CATEGORY SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS (1)-(8) (PDF 165) are recorded verbatim, numeric or not, plus every per-section SPECIAL REQUIREMENT / RESTRICTION / SOLO prerequisite that carries a measurable value. 'numbers' is {} for the purely qualitative ones.

The MIF «2» prerequisite for practicing maneuvers on the SOLO sortie is printed three times and all three are recorded: PDF 179 (C49XX, item 3.a — Aileron Roll / Chandelle / Lazy «8»), PDF 186 (C52XX, item 3.c) and PDF 188 (C53XX, item 3.c). It is the same threshold type as General Directive (4) (min_mif_normal_landing: 2) and uses the key 'min_mif_previous_dual_contact'. Note the wording differs between 186 ('permitted for SOLO') and 188 ('allowed for SOLO') — preserved verbatim.
